segments.say: Hitler's order was to yield not a yard of ground, and to show his troops no other road than that to victory or death.
segments.caption: Hitler's order: yield not a yard of ground, and show the troops no other road than that to victory or death.

segments.say: November fourth, nineteen forty two. El Alamein, Egypt.
segments.caption: 4 November 1942. El Alamein, Egypt.

segments.say: The order reached Rommel the afternoon before. We were completely stunned, he wrote. He obeyed, and ordered his men to hold.
segments.caption: The order reached Rommel the afternoon before. "We were completely stunned," he wrote. He obeyed, and ordered his men to hold.

segments.say: On the morning of November fourth, the British broke through. Rommel wrote that by early afternoon, a nineteen kilometre hole had been burst in his front.
segments.caption: On the morning of 4 November, the British broke through. By early afternoon, Rommel wrote, a 19 kilometre hole had been burst in his front.

segments.say: That same day, General fon Toe mah, commander of the Afrika Korps, was captured. Montgomery met him, and later invited him to dinner.
segments.caption: That same day General Wilhelm Ritter von Thoma, commander of the Afrika Korps, was captured. Montgomery met him, and later invited him to dinner.

segments.say: At five thirty that evening, Rommel ordered a general retreat without waiting for Hitler's reply. He had to save what could be saved.
segments.caption: At 17:30 Rommel ordered a general retreat without waiting for Hitler's reply. He had to save what could be saved.

segments.say: With little transport, much of the Italian infantry was left behind. About thirty thousand Axis soldiers were taken prisoner in the battle.
segments.caption: With little transport, much of the Italian infantry was left behind. About 30,000 Axis soldiers were taken prisoner in the battle.

segments.say: On November fifteenth, church bells rang across Britain for its first great land victory over the German army.
segments.caption: On 15 November, church bells rang across Britain for its first great land victory over the German army.

segments.say: Churchill said: Now this is not the end. It is not even the beginning of the end. But it is, perhaps, the end of the beginning.
segments.caption: Churchill: "Now this is not the end. It is not even the beginning of the end. But it is, perhaps, the end of the beginning."
